dialogue.content: こんにちは、相談員です
dialogue.English: Hello, I'm the counselor.

dialogue.content: 相談にお越しいただき、ありがとうございます
dialogue.English: Thank you for coming in for a consultation today.

dialogue.content: 最初に、年齢、性別、ご相談内容を教えてください
dialogue.English: To begin, could you please tell me your age, gender, and what you'd like to discuss?

dialogue.content: 16歳　女性です。進路について悩んでいることがあります。
dialogue.English: I'm 16 years old, female. I have concerns about my future path.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。それは悩みますね進路のどんなことをお悩みですか？
dialogue.English: I see. That can certainly be a difficult thing to think about. What specifically about your future path is concerning you?

dialogue.content: 小さい頃から薬剤師はいいと母から言われ、理系に進みましたが、本当に薬剤師になりたいのかなと自問自答してしまいます。
dialogue.English: Ever since I was little, my mother told me that being a pharmacist is a good job, so I chose the science track, but I keep asking myself if I really want to become a pharmacist.

dialogue.content: かといってやりたいこともなく、考える度に何のために生きているのかと、進路以上のとこまで考えてしまうこともあって。
dialogue.English: But then again, I don't have anything else I particularly want to do, and every time I think about it, I go beyond just my future path and end up pondering bigger questions, like what I'm even living for.

dialogue.content: ええ、それは考えてしまいますね・・・
dialogue.English: Yes, it's understandable that your thoughts would go there...

dialogue.content: はい。
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 今、16歳ということは、高校1年ですか？2年生ですか？
dialogue.English: You're 16—are you in your first year of high school? Or second?

dialogue.content: 高校2年生です。
dialogue.English: I'm in my second year of high school.

dialogue.content: では、そろそろ進路を絞る時期ですよね
dialogue.English: So, it's about time to start narrowing down your options for the future, isn't it?

dialogue.content: 薬剤師さんということは、理系だと思いますが、文系と理系では、どちらが得意ですか？
dialogue.English: Since you mentioned being a pharmacist, that's in the science field. Between liberal arts and the sciences, which do you feel more comfortable with?

dialogue.content: はい。進路相談で先生と面談しましたが、家に帰ってから、本当にいいのかと考えています。
dialogue.English: Yes. I had a guidance session with my teacher, but after I got home, I started wondering if it's really the right choice for me.

dialogue.content: 化学が好きなので理系が得意です。
dialogue.English: I like chemistry, so I'm better at the sciences.

dialogue.content: では、進路の方向としては、理系でも大丈夫なんですね
dialogue.English: So, in terms of your general direction, the science track would be fine for you, then?

dialogue.content: それが自分でもわからなくて…。理系は好きですが、その道をやりたいかといったら、なんか違うような。
dialogue.English: That's what I don't know myself... I like the sciences, but when I ask myself if I want to pursue a career in it, it feels like something is off.

dialogue.content: うまく説明できなくてすみません。
dialogue.English: I'm sorry I can't explain it well.

dialogue.content: うんうん、わかります。いやとまでは思わないけれど、本当にやりたいことなのかどうかがわからないんですよね
dialogue.English: Mhm, I understand. It's not that you dislike it, but you're just not sure if it's what you truly want to do, right?

dialogue.content: はい。
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 誰かに相談してみましたか？
dialogue.English: Have you talked to anyone about this?

dialogue.content: いえ、周りの友人も進路が決まっていて、自分だけがまだハッキリしていないです。
dialogue.English: No, my friends around me have already decided on their paths, and I'm the only one who's still undecided.

dialogue.content: それは、焦りますよね
dialogue.English: That must make you feel anxious, right?

dialogue.content: はい、小さい頃から言われたし、先生からも薬剤師になれるからと言われたので、自分のやりたいことがわからないです。
dialogue.English: Yes, it's what I've been told since I was little, and even my teacher said I could become a pharmacist, so I don't know what I want to do for myself.

dialogue.content: 兄がいますが、兄は母の言われたように進み、やりたいことを諦めて、たまに自傷行為をしています。
dialogue.English: I have an older brother. He followed what our mother told him to do, gave up on what he wanted to do, and sometimes he engages in self-harm.

dialogue.content: うんうん、悩みますよね。他に興味のあるものは今のところないっておっしゃっていましたよね
dialogue.English: Mm-hm, it's understandable to struggle with that. You mentioned that at the moment, you don't have any other interests, correct?

dialogue.content: はい。
dialogue.English: That's right.

dialogue.content: お兄さんは、何かを諦められたんですねそれを見ている分、本当にやりたいことって何かを考えてしまいますよね
dialogue.English: So your brother had to give something up. Seeing that must make you think even more about what you truly want to do.

dialogue.content: 高校2年生ということだけど、進路の決定はいつ頃が最終決定なのですか？
dialogue.English: You said you're a second-year in high school; when is the final deadline for deciding on your future path?

dialogue.content: （リオンさん、実は織田です。ちょっと、もう一組の方を見てきたいので、少しお待ちいただけますか？）
dialogue.English: (Rion-san, this is actually Oda. I need to go check on the other group for a moment, could you please wait a bit?)

dialogue.content: 兄は宗教等の歴史に興味があったのですが、そういう学校は良くないとかで諦めてました。
dialogue.English: My brother was interested in the history of religion and such, but he gave up because he was told that schools for that kind of thing weren't good.

dialogue.content: 承知しました。
dialogue.English: Understood.

dialogue.content: 最終決定は3学期が終わる頃なので、来年の3月になります。
dialogue.English: The final decision is due around the end of the third semester, so that would be next March.

dialogue.content: 教えてくれてありがとうございます
dialogue.English: Thank you for letting me know.

dialogue.content: お兄さんは、やりたいことを諦めたこと、後悔されているのかもしれませんね
dialogue.English: Your brother may regret giving up what he wanted to do.

dialogue.content: でも、あなたはまだ時間があるので、じっくり考えることはできると思います
dialogue.English: But you still have time, so I think you can take your time to think it through.

dialogue.content: 兄はあまり口数が少ないのでわからないですが、おそらく後悔しているかもしれません。
dialogue.English: My brother doesn't talk much so I don't know for sure, but he probably does regret it.

dialogue.content: そうかもしれませんね。その姿を見ていたら、あなたも色々と思うところはありますよね
dialogue.English: That might be the case. Seeing him like that must give you a lot to think about, too.

dialogue.content: もし、薬剤師さんじゃない進路を選ぼうと思ったら、それをご両親とお話できそうですか？
dialogue.English: If you were to choose a path other than becoming a pharmacist, do you think you could talk with your parents about it?

dialogue.content: 時間があると思っていても、つい焦ってしまいます。
dialogue.English: Even though I know I have time, I can't help but feel rushed.

dialogue.content: 焦る気持ちは、もちろんあると思います。自然なことですよ
dialogue.English: It's completely understandable to feel rushed. That's perfectly normal.

dialogue.content: 話せなくはないですが、母はあーだこーだ言ってきそうで。
dialogue.English: It's not that I can't talk to her, but my mother would probably have a lot to say about it.

dialogue.content: うんうん・・・薬剤師になりなさいって言いそうですか？
dialogue.English: Mm-hm... Do you think she would tell you to become a pharmacist?

dialogue.content: 言いそうです。もったいないと言われます。
dialogue.English: She probably would. She'd say it's a waste.

dialogue.content: 父ならやりたいようにすればいいという人なので話せるかも。
dialogue.English: My father is the type to say 'do what you want to do,' so I might be able to talk to him.

dialogue.content: なるほど、お父さんの方が話ができそうなんですね
dialogue.English: I see, so it seems like it would be easier to talk to your father.

dialogue.content: はい、なんて言ってくるかわからないですが、母よりはまだ…。
dialogue.English: Yes, I'm not sure what he'd say, but it would be better than talking to my mother...

dialogue.content: そうなんですね・・まず、実は迷っているってこと、お父さんにはお話できそう？
dialogue.English: I see... For starters, do you think you could tell your father that you're actually feeling unsure?

dialogue.content: 話はできそうです。普段仕事で朝早く夜も遅いので、休みの日にはなってしまいますが。
dialogue.English: I think I could talk to him. He usually leaves early for work and comes home late, so it would have to be on his day off.

dialogue.content: うんうん、そうなんですねいきなり「こういう進路にする」というよりも、今迷っている気持ちをお話しておいた方がよくないかな？と思ったんですが、いかがですか？
dialogue.English: Mhm, I see. I was thinking that rather than suddenly saying, 'I've decided on this path,' it might be better to first tell him about the uncertainty you're feeling right now. What do you think?

dialogue.content: そうですね。決まってはいないけど、気持ちを伝えておくのはいいのかも。
dialogue.English: That makes sense. It might be good to let him know how I'm feeling, even if I haven't decided yet.

dialogue.content: それと、お父さんに、それとなくお母さんってどう思うかな？とか、迷っていること、言っておいてくれないかな？という風にお願いしてみるのも一つですよ
dialogue.English: Also, you could try asking your father, perhaps indirectly, what he thinks your mother would say, or even ask him if he could mention to her that you're feeling unsure. That's one option.

dialogue.content: 父はわかってくれるかもしれないですが、両親の仲が悪くて、父と母は全く話さないので、難しいかも。
dialogue.English: My father might understand, but my parents don't get along, and they don't talk to each other at all, so that might be difficult.

dialogue.content: 多分喧嘩します。
dialogue.English: They would probably fight.

dialogue.content: そうだったんですねあなたは、お母さんに反対されたら、やりたいって思ったことを諦めてしまいそうですか？あきらめたくありませんか？
dialogue.English: I see. If your mother opposed it, do you think you might give up on what you want to do? Or would you rather not give up?

dialogue.content: （もう一つの方を見てくるので、ちょっとお待ちくださいね）
dialogue.English: (I'm going to check on the other group, so please wait a moment.)

dialogue.content: 諦めてしまうかもしれないです。兄と同じ道になるのかな。
dialogue.English: I might end up giving up. I wonder if I'll end up on the same path as my brother.

dialogue.content: そう感じるんですね・・・諦めたくないお気持ちはありますか？例えば、誰かが応援してくれるとか
dialogue.English: That's how it feels to you... Is there also a part of you that doesn't want to give up? For example, if someone were to support you.

dialogue.content: ありますね。自分の人生なので。
dialogue.English: I do. It's my own life, after all.

dialogue.content: ええ、それは大事なお気持ちですよね。諦めたくないって、大事なことだと思います
dialogue.English: Yes, that's a very important feeling. I think not wanting to give up is a crucial thing.

dialogue.content: 30代40代になってからやっぱりやってみたいというのと今からやってみるのでは違いますよね？
dialogue.English: Realizing you want to do something in your 30s or 40s and starting it then is different from starting now, isn't it?

dialogue.content: 今からやるのと、30代40代からやるのは違うというのは・・？
dialogue.English: When you say it's different to start now versus in your 30s or 40s, you mean...?

dialogue.content: 頑張って説得してみようかな。
dialogue.English: Maybe I should try hard to persuade them.

dialogue.content: 自分の人生って、やっぱりどういう風に生きていくか、自分が公開しないって大事なことだと思います
dialogue.English: When it comes to your own life, I think it's important to live it in a way that you won't have any regrets.

dialogue.content: 公開→後悔、です。ごめんなさい
dialogue.English: I meant 'regret,' not 'public.' Sorry about that.

dialogue.content: 大人になってからやり始めるより早くにやっていた方が知識の量や経験も違ってくるのかなと思って。
dialogue.English: I feel that starting earlier, rather than waiting until I'm an adult, would make a difference in the amount of knowledge and experience I would gain.

dialogue.content: はい、おっしゃる通りですね
dialogue.English: Yes, you're absolutely right.

dialogue.content: まずは父に相談してみます。
dialogue.English: I'll start by talking with my father.

dialogue.content: まだ時間はあります。ちゃんと考えて、お父さんや学校の先生にもいろいろ聞いて相談しながらやってみてください
dialogue.English: You still have time. Please think it through carefully, and try talking and consulting with your father and your teachers at school.

dialogue.content: はい、ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Okay, thank you very much.

dialogue.content: 行き違いましたね💦ええ、ご相談してみてくださいね
dialogue.English: Our messages must have crossed. Yes, please do try consulting with them.

dialogue.content: 今日はいかがでしたか？
dialogue.English: How are you feeling about our session today?
